raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches and my changes comply.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL (FROST SDPA forward placement, SM107 (Rubin) half row only).

## Summary

`_place_sm107_f16` led the backend only for a selected native THD split or the qualified packed paged prefill. Every dense graph therefore ran on the backend, including decode-shaped and d512 shapes where the backend is 2-10x slower on Rubin.

For dense graphs on cc 10.7 (no THD, paging, window or sink), this PR adds the measured shards:
- **`2 <= s_q <= 16`**:
  - d192/d256/d512 lead.
  - d64/d128 lead at one KV unit, or at up to 8 KV units with at least 8k KV.
- **Prefill**:
  - d512 and its envelope lead.
  - Chunks of at most 128 Q tiles from a 4k cache lead. These are the SM100 chunk bounds (`CHUNKED_MAX_Q_TILES`, `CHUNKED_MIN_KV_TOKENS`).
- **Unchanged**: squares, wider chunks and `s_q == 1` keep the backend first.

## Why

Setup: gr100 board (cc 10.7, 216 SMs), public cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CuTeDSL 4.8.0. I timed the backend's pick against the first FROST plan with CUDA-graph replay, warm and with an L2 flush, as the median of 11.

There were 620 dense BF16 cases: decode (`s_q` 1 and 4), chunked prefill, squares, the d512 envelope (d320-d448), and a random hold-out.

| Shard | FROST / backend |
|---|---|
| `s_q` 2-16, d192 / d256 / d512 | 0.04-0.75 / 0.08-0.42 / 0.19-0.33 |
| `s_q` 2-16, d64/d128, <= 8 KV units with >= 8k KV, or 1 unit | 0.07-0.63 |
| `s_q` 2-16, d64/d128, 64+ units | 0.91-1.62 (TRAIL) |
| prefill d512 + envelope | 0.08-0.67 |
| chunk, <= 128 Q tiles, >= 4k KV (d64-d256) | 0.04-1.00 |
| squares d64-d256, wider chunks | 0.42-1.98, mixed (TRAIL) |
| `s_q == 1` (d64/d128/d256/d512) | 1.6-25 (TRAIL) |

| Placement | Leads | Mean regret | Leads slower than 1.03x |
|---|---|---|---|
| develop | 0 | 116% | 0 |
| this PR | 224 | 3.2% | 0 |

Measurement caveats:
- On this board the first-measured arm (FROST) can read 40-85% slow on an otherwise identical plan. That biases every ratio above against FROST, so a lead this rule takes is, if anything, understated.
- Another user's jobs shared the GPU for part of the session. Those phases (THD sets, the tail of the d512 envelope sweep, one chunk pass) were discarded, and every number above is from minutes with no other process on the GPU.
- The split-KV cost constants were not refit for Rubin. The fit tool showed that the floor and minimum-tiles constants do not change Rubin's picks, and the board's noise is too high for 10-30% split comparisons.

Not changed: `s_q == 1` d192, which wins 0.37-0.84 only at 128 KV units and needs a wider sweep. Also unchanged are THD, paged, windowed and sink graphs, and the FP8/MXFP8 Rubin rows.

## API and compatibility impact

Only the default plan order for SM107 f16/bf16 dense graphs changes. Explicit knob records and the opt-in flag behave as before.

## Testing

- Heuristics / placement / split-KV / analyzer host tests: 1571 passed, 2 skipped.
- No new unit test pins these bounds (test/AGENTS.md); the measurements above are the evidence.

---

@@ -110,8 +110,17 @@
 
 SM107 half uses the shared paged/nonpaged native THD split selectors and the
 measured packed-GQA paged prefill contract. Selected native splits retain
-priority; other eligible graphs retain the backend first. The per-tensor FP8
-Rubin row remains opt-in. Qualification and timing evidence are maintained internally.
+priority. Dense graphs (no THD, paging, window or sink), measured 2026-10-08 on a gr100 board
+(216 SMs) against public cuDNN 9.27.0.42, 620 cases (decode, chunked prefill, squares, d512
+envelope, random hold-out); develop led none of them (mean regret 116%):
+- ``2 <= s_q <= 16``: d192/d256/d512 lead (0.04-0.75; the backend runs these 2-10x slower);
+  d64/d128 lead at one KV unit or <= 8 units with >= 8k KV (0.07-0.63), 64+ units lose 1.1-1.6x.
+- prefill: d512 and its envelope lead (0.08-0.67); chunks of <= 128 Q tiles from a 4k cache lead
+  (d64-d256, 0.04-1.00). Squares and wider chunks are mixed (up to 1.98x) -> TRAIL.
+- ``s_q == 1`` keeps the backend (d64/d128/d256/d512 1.6-25x; d192 mixed).
+New mean regret 3.2%, no lead slower than 1.03x warm or cold. The board's timing is noisy for the
+first arm measured (FROST), which biases these ratios against FROST. The per-tensor FP8
+Rubin row remains opt-in.
 
 SM107 MXFP8 row (``sdpa_fwd_prefill_sm107_mxfp8``, offered by default since 2026-10): LEAD on exact
 cc 10.7 for every graph the row admits -- dense BSHD, exact d128 / d192x128 / d256 / d512, E4M3 / E5M2
@@ -205,6 +214,8 @@
 
 # SM120 f16/bf16 thresholds.
 SM120_SQ1_MIN_KV_UNITS = 8  # s_q == 1: b * h_kv below this (b = 1) loses 1.13-1.85 on every head dim
+SM107_DECODE_SHAPED_MAX_UNITS = 8  # 2 <= s_q <= 16, d64/d128: b * h_kv above this lost to the backend
+SM107_DECODE_SHAPED_MIN_KV_TOKENS = 8192  # ... and at 8 units a 2k cache is parity (0.91-1.06)
 SM120_SQ1_D256_MIN_KV_UNITS = 12  # s_q == 1, d256: 8 units at 2k KV lost 1.55x; 12+ ran 0.74-1.04 (cuDNN 9.27)
 SM120_SQ1_MAX_GQA_GROUP = 64  # s_q == 1, d512: a 128-wide query group over one KV head loses 5-10x at every batch
 
@@ -227,8 +238,8 @@ def place(spec, facts) -> str:
     """``LEAD`` or ``TRAIL`` for the row ``spec`` serving ``facts`` (see the module docstring).
 
     Keyed by the row's name: the SM100, SM120 and SM90 f16/bf16 rows and the SM100 FP8 row each use
-    their measured shard table. The SM107 half row leads for a selected native THD split
-    or qualified packed paged prefill; the SM107 MXFP8 row leads on exact cc 10.7 for every graph it
+    their measured shard table. The SM107 half row leads for a selected native THD split,
+    qualified packed paged prefill, or the measured dense shards; the SM107 MXFP8 row leads on exact cc 10.7 for every graph it
     admits (a qualification verdict, module docstring). Every unmeasured row (SM80, SM100 mxfp8, the
     fp8 rows of SM107 / SM120) keeps the historical order -- those stay opt-in, so the order is only
     observable with the flag set, which ranks ours first anyway."""
@@ -258,6 +269,20 @@ def _place_sm107_f16(caps: Capabilities, facts) -> str:
     # Share the qualified prefix envelope with candidate generation.
     if paged_d256_prefix_launch(caps, facts) is not None or nonpaged_thd_split_choice(caps, facts)[0] > 1 or paged_thd_split_choice(caps, facts)[0] > 1:
         return LEAD
+    if not (facts.thd or facts.has_paged_kv or facts.has_sink) and facts.window_left is None:
+        # Dense, measured on a gr100 board (216 SMs) against cuDNN 9.27 (2026-10-08).
+        flavor = _selected_d_shape(caps, facts)
+        if 2 <= facts.s_q <= DECODE_SHAPED_MAX_S_Q:
+            if flavor in ((192, 128), (256, 256), (512, 512)):
+                return LEAD  # 0.04-0.75 of the backend
+            units = facts.b * facts.h_kv
+            if units == 1 or (units <= SM107_DECODE_SHAPED_MAX_UNITS and facts.s_kv >= SM107_DECODE_SHAPED_MIN_KV_TOKENS):
+                return LEAD  # d64/d128: 0.07-0.63; 64+ units lost 1.1-1.6x
+        elif facts.s_q > DECODE_SHAPED_MAX_S_Q:
+            if flavor == (512, 512):
+                return LEAD  # d512 and its d320-d448 envelope: 0.08-0.67
+            if facts.s_q < facts.s_kv and facts.s_kv >= CHUNKED_MIN_KV_TOKENS and _q_tiles(facts) <= CHUNKED_MAX_Q_TILES:
+                return LEAD  # chunked, d64-d256: 0.04-1.00; squares and wider chunks stay mixed (up to 1.98x)
     # The shared paged pipeline also benefits from GQA packing without a
     # split. Large-batch short queries recover unused Q rows without partials.
     # Smaller GPU-only gains do not reliably repay the host submission cost;

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `d3c9f84e1dba`; no actionable finding. The one-file placement change preserves admission/filtering and the backend fallback. Integration with current develop `eae67e3b9f78` is clean.

Validation: **1,057 host tests passed** (two cases deselected). Actual-source comparison across 24,192 modeled cases changes 3,520 SM107 choices only; 180 additional THD/paged/window/sink/architecture controls preserve prior placement. Sampled 114 complete proposals and checked all 160 returned candidates for admission and a single trailing backend marker.

**14 native SM107 cases passed** with automatic dispatch and both force-provider flags removed: FP16/BF16 decode-shaped d64/d128/d192/d256, d512 and d320-envelope prefill, and a d128 chunk. Each selected engine 20515, matched full chunked FP64 O/LSE references, and passed poisoned-output capture replay after changing Q/V.

An idle-board ABBA spot check compared parent versus new automatic placement on identical source/dependencies (216-SM Rubin, cuDNN 9.27.0.28). Both policies passed the same numerical/replay checks. Median warm GPU replay times, in microseconds:

| BF16 workload, B1/H8 | Parent | New |
|---|---:|---:|
| d64, Hkv1, Q4/KV512 | 15.8 | 14.5 |
| d512, Hkv8, Q17/KV512 | 34.6 | 13.9 |
| d128, Hkv8, Q256/KV4096 | 42.2 | 26.5 |

Host enqueue medians were about 9 microseconds for the backend and unsplit d512 path, versus 13 microseconds for the two new split paths. These are three warm cases, not independent reproduction of the author's full sweep or cold-cache claims. Compilation/setup was excluded.

Owner-started pipeline **72572310** is running on this head; pending CI is not counted as passing, and no duplicate run was requested.
